title: [VSC-17] CI: package the VS Code extension on every PR and smoke-test its bundle
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-16 (task-6fbd08111de142508fb0402d06f24e3f): the smoke checks the packaged .vsix against the scripts/bundle-manifest.json that VSC-16 creates.

Objective: pull requests never package the VS Code extension. In .github/workflows/ci.yml, job build-all-platforms, the step "Test VS Code daemon startup" runs only npm ci, lint, compile and test; `npm run package` runs only in release.yml, so a packaging break surfaces at release time. The JetBrains job already packages and runs `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs` on the unzipped plugin.

Deliverable:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: in build-all-platforms on ubuntu-latest only (the job builds daemon and proxy earlier), after the VS Code tests: `npm run package` in moe-vscode, unzip the .vsix to "$RUNNER_TEMP/moe-vscode-smoke", run `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/moe-vscode-smoke/extension/bundled"`, and fail when any file the bundle manifest lists is missing from the vsix.
- moe-vscode/.vscodeignore: stop shipping the tsc output that `npm run compile` leaves in dist/ beside esbuild's dist/extension.js (exclude dist/** except dist/extension.js), and eslint.config.mjs. At 882a4c39, packaging after a compile shipped dist/panels, dist/providers, dist/services and the rest.

Shared file: .github/workflows/ci.yml is also planned by open rows outside this epic (task-3ad573a7, task-4fdc7590, task-f6228433 when this row was cut). In shared-checkout mode do not run concurrently with them; after the worktree switch non-overlapping hunks merge on their own.

Not in scope: release.yml, the Windows and macOS legs (Linux is enough for a packaging smoke), any other CI step.

Verification: in a git-archive snapshot outside the checkout whose absolute path has NO UUID-shaped segment (npm 12 redacts UUIDs in `npm list` output and vsce then packages nothing; see VSC-16), e.g. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/vsc17-<sha>: build daemon and proxy, run `cd moe-vscode && npm ci && npm run compile`, then the new CI step's commands verbatim from the snapshot root; show `unzip -Z1 <vsix> | grep '^extension/dist/'` lists only extension.js; and `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))'` exits 0 (PyYAML 6.0.1 is installed).
definitionOfDone: .github/workflows/ci.yml's build-all-platforms job runs, on ubuntu-latest only, `npm run package` in moe-vscode after the existing VS Code tests, then the onboarding smoke on the unzipped vsix's extension/bundled dir and a check that every file scripts/bundle-manifest.json lists is in the vsix.

moe-vscode/.vscodeignore excludes dist/** except dist/extension.js, and eslint.config.mjs; in a snapshot, `npm run compile && npm run package` yields a vsix whose only extension/dist/ entry is extension.js (listing in the summary).
The new CI commands, run verbatim in a UUID-free git-archive snapshot after the daemon and proxy builds, exit 0 (output tail in the summary).
The diff touches only .github/workflows/ci.yml and moe-vscode/.vscodeignore.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-vscode/.vscodeignore (DoD 2): stop shipping the tsc output that `npm run compile` leaves in dist/ beside esbuild's dist/extension.js, and the top-level eslint.config.mjs. Use the Edit tool (GLOBAL rail: no shell writes to tracked files). Append exactly these four lines after the last line (`scripts/**`), LF, final newline, no other line touched:

# `npm run compile` leaves tsc output in dist/ beside the esbuild bundle; ship only dist/extension.js (VSC-17).
dist/**
!dist/extension.js
eslint.config.mjs

Why this works (mem:gotcha-vsce-vscodeignore-negations-win): vsce 4.0.0 (node_modules/@vscode/vsce/out/package.js, collectFiles ~1360-1378) splits the patterns into an ignore list and a negate list. A file ships when it matches NO ignore pattern or ANY negate pattern, so line order is irrelevant: `!dist/extension.js` keeps the bundle wherever it sits. Keep `!bundled/**` and `!bundled/**/*` exactly as they are. They are why every staged bundle file ships despite `**/*.ts`, `**/*.map` and `**/*.log`. dist/extension.js.map stays out through the existing `**/*.map`. `eslint.config.mjs` has no leading `**/`, so it is anchored at the extension root. The 8 dependency eslint.config.js files under bundled/daemon/node_modules keep shipping, which is expected. Planning run at ff56d4ff: this exact change removes 21 tsc dist/*.js files and eslint.config.mjs from `vsce ls` and nothing else (checkRef 5). Error handling: none applies in an ignore file. The proof is the step 3 tests (checkRefs 3 and 5).
implementationPlan.note: Appended the comment, dist/**, !dist/extension.js and eslint.config.mjs to moe-vscode/.vscodeignore with the Edit tool. All existing lines untouched, including !bundled/** and !bundled/**/*. Proof is in step 3 (checkRefs 3 and 5). Dirty peer paths in the shared checkout (.moe/roles, .moe/skills, board json) left alone.

Inserted the step "Package the VS Code extension and smoke-test its bundle" after "Test VS Code daemon startup" in build-all-platforms, via the Edit tool, verbatim from the plan (if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest', shell: bash, quoted CHECK heredoc). yaml.safe_load exit 0; checkRef 2 printed "step 20 ok"; no tabs; ci.yml +46/-0. Full end-to-end proof is step 3.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY ONCE, fresh, after steps 1-2 (DoD 2, 3, 4 and 5). Run the checkRefs in order from the checkout root, exactly as written: 1 and 2 (YAML parse; placement right after "Test VS Code daemon startup" and `if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'`), 3 (end-to-end snapshot), 4 (negative control), 5 (vsce ls diff), 6 (diff scope).
- GLOBAL rail: never build, install or test in the checkout. checkRef 3 runs `git archive HEAD`, overlays your two edited files (cp --parents), and runs everything in $HOME/moe-scratch/vsc17-<sha>-<epoch>. That is ext4 and UUID-free. Under a Claude scratchpad path npm 12 redacts the UUID segment and vsce packs nothing (mem:gotcha-vsce-package-uuid-path). It also records the path in $HOME/moe-scratch/vsc17-last for checkRefs 4 and 5.

- A real failure is a finding, never something to filter. Example: the check names a manifest target that the bundler never stages or vsce drops. Fix it if the cause is in the two task files; otherwise comment on this row naming the path and stop. Never weaken the check, the negative control or the manifest.
- Never pattern-kill. Onboarding stops only its own daemon and proxy. The snapshot is about 0.8 GB: remove it only by its exact recorded path if your harness allows, else name it in the summary.
- complete_task evidence: checkRef 3's command, exit code and output tail. Summary: the dist/eslint lines (DoD 2), the `All 16 ...` and PASS lines (DoD 3), checkRef 4's three lines, checkRef 5's diff, the yaml exit 0 (DoD 4), and the git diff --stat of the two files (DoD 5, about +50 lines).

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff, with the adversarial-self-review skill. Answer each point in the step note:
(a) vsce semantics: name every pattern you added, and say why `!bundled/**` and `!bundled/**/*` stay. checkRef 5 must show only removals of dist/ tsc output and eslint.config.mjs.
(b) Fail-closed paths, each one tested in checkRef 4 or by reasoning against the code: empty listing, manifest with no copies, `into` with a trailing slash (posix join), a `files` copy whose file never staged, an empty staged directory, malformed JSON. Is any reachable path an exit 0 on a missing file?
(c) CI mechanics: the step runs only on ubuntu-latest; RUNNER_TEMP is per job; `set -euo pipefail` with `unzip -Z1 > file`; the heredoc terminator at column 0 after YAML strips the indent; no `${{` inside the JS; the job's earlier `npm install` (daemon, proxy) and `npm ci` (moe-vscode) cover what vscode:prepublish needs.
(d) Cross-platform: Windows and macOS legs skip the step; nothing else in the job changes. Size: git diff --numstat of the two files (about +50; the QA cap is 400). Scope: you touched only ci.yml and .vscodeignore (git status --short -- <the two paths>). Never revert, stash, git add -A or commit a peer's dirty path in this shared checkout.
Error handling: a finding gets a fix in the two task files plus a fresh re-run of the affected checkRef. It is never waved through.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of the two-file diff (ci.yml +46, .vscodeignore +4, no other path touched by me).
(a) vsce: added `dist/**`, `!dist/extension.js`, `eslint.config.mjs` (plus one comment line). `!bundled/**` and `!bundled/**/*` stay untouched: they are why every staged bundle file ships despite `**/*.ts`, `**/*.map`, `**/*.log`, and the check depends on that. checkRef 5 (fresh): only 21 removed dist/*.js tsc files and eslint.config.mjs; nothing added, nothing else removed.
(b) Fail-closed, probed fresh by running the extracted CHECK script (scratch, outside the checkout) on hostile inputs: empty listing -> `Nothing to compare: 0 vsix entries`, exit 1; `{"copies":[]}` and `{}` -> `Nothing to compare ... 0 targets`, exit 1; malformed JSON -> Node throws, exit 1; `into` "scripts/" (trailing slash) -> resolves as the staged dir, exit 0 only because all its files ship (correct); a `files` copy whose file never staged -> `Missing from the vsix: extension/bundled/scripts/neverstaged.mjs`, exit 1; empty staged dir -> `(nothing staged)`, exit 1; `..` into -> `(not bundle-relative)`, exit 1; missing `into` -> `undefined (not bundle-relative)`, exit 1; one shipped file (docs/roles/qa.md) dropped from the listing -> named, exit 1; good input -> `All 16 ...`, exit 0. No reachable path exits 0 with a manifest target missing. Residual by design: a file the bundler never staged and that is not a `files` target is invisible to the check; bundle-assets.mjs refuses that before packaging, and the `required` flag stays the bundler's job.
(c) CI mechanics: step is ubuntu-only (`if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'`); explicit `shell: bash` gives -eo pipefail; RUNNER_TEMP is set by the runner; `unzip -Z1 > file` fails the step on error; the heredoc terminator CHECK lands at column 0 (the step.sh extracted through yaml.safe_load ran green); no `${{` in the JS (grep empty), so Actions interpolates nothing; earlier steps Build daemon/Build proxy (npm install + build) and Test VS Code daemon startup (npm ci + compile) cover vscode:prepublish, same chain release.yml uses.
(d) Windows and macOS legs skip the step; no other step or job changed. Size +50 lines against the 400 cap. git status --short on the two paths: ` M` each. Dirty peer paths (.moe/roles, .moe/skills, board json) were not touched, reverted, stashed or staged. Theoretical only: onboarding's 20 s restart-health deadline can trip on a very slow disk (CI runners are ext4; I did not edit onboarding.mjs); a future vsce upgrade changing ignore semantics would make checkRefs 4 and 5 fail loudly. No findings required a fix.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: On every pull request, the ubuntu-latest leg of build-all-platforms packages moe-vscode with `npm run package`. The leg fails with a named path when any scripts/bundle-manifest.json target is missing from the .vsix: for a files copy each <into>/<name>, for a directory copy every file bundle-assets.mjs staged under <into>. The leg then runs scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs against the packaged extension/bundled. The vsix ships dist/extension.js as its only dist/ entry and no top-level eslint.config.mjs, and every other file it shipped before still ships.
acceptanceCriteria: build-all-platforms has a step named exactly "Package the VS Code extension and smoke-test its bundle", immediately after "Test VS Code daemon startup", with `if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'` and `shell: bash` (checkRef 2).

The step runs `npm run package -- --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/moe-vscode.vsix"` in moe-vscode, then the inline manifest check, then unzips to "$RUNNER_TEMP/moe-vscode-smoke" and runs `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/moe-vscode-smoke/extension/bundled"`; run verbatim in a UUID-free snapshot it exits 0 (checkRef 3).

The check prints `Missing from the vsix: extension/bundled/<path>` once per missing path and exits 1. It exits 1 with `Nothing to compare:` on an empty listing or when there are no targets. On success it prints `All <n> bundle-manifest.json targets are in the vsix` (n = 16 at 84536308).
The packaged vsix's only entries matching ^extension/(dist/|eslint) are exactly extension/dist/extension.js (checkRef 3).
Dropping the !bundled negations and excluding bundled/docs/roles/qa.md makes the step exit non-zero, naming extension/bundled/docs/roles/qa.md (checkRef 4).
`vsce ls` under the new .vscodeignore differs from the base only by removed dist/ tsc files and eslint.config.mjs (checkRef 5).
python3 yaml.safe_load of ci.yml exits 0 (checkRef 1), and the task's commits touch only the two files plus board JSON (checkRef 6).
invariants: The check never re-implements the Ant exclude rules: directory targets are compared against the staged copy in moe-vscode/bundled.
The check fails closed: no reachable path exits 0 while a manifest target is missing from the vsix.
No build, install or test runs in the shared checkout; tracked files are written only with the Edit tool; no process is pattern-killed.
compatibility: release.yml, every other ci.yml step and job, and the windows-latest and macos-latest legs stay byte-identical in behaviour.
Every existing .vscodeignore line stays, including `!bundled/**` and `!bundled/**/*`. The vsix keeps every file it shipped before except dist/ tsc output and eslint.config.mjs.
scripts/bundle-manifest.json is read as VSC-16 landed it (copies/from/into/files/required/exclude) and is never edited.
approvedScope: The one new CI step as written in step 2: name, if, shell, and the run block with its inline ESM check. The check's CLI is: manifest path, listing file, staged root.
Four appended .vscodeignore lines: one comment, then dist/**, !dist/extension.js and eslint.config.mjs.
reuse: scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs, invoked exactly as release.yml's "Verify packaged onboarding" and the JetBrains job invoke it.
moe-vscode's `npm run package` (vsce package, whose vscode:prepublish runs bundle-assets.mjs and esbuild), with vsce's --out flag.
VSC-16's bundle-assets.mjs staging as the source of truth for directory targets; Node 24 fs.readdirSync({recursive, withFileTypes}); unzip -Z1.
sourceAssumptions: vsce 4.0.0 node_modules/@vscode/vsce/out/package.js collectFiles (~1360-1378): ignore and negate lists; a file ships when it matches no ignore or any negate; minimatch {dot:true}.
moe-vscode/package.json: package = `vsce package`; vscode:prepublish = `npm run bundle && npm run esbuild`; esbuild writes dist/extension.js with --sourcemap.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A committed scripts/tests/ check file was rejected: DoD 5 limits the diff to ci.yml and .vscodeignore, so the check lives inline as a quoted heredoc. (2) Re-applying the manifest `exclude` globs to the source dirs was rejected: it would be a third copy of the Ant rules (bundle-assets.mjs antPattern, Gradle exclude()) that can drift. Comparing against the staged moe-vscode/bundled copy needs none. (3) A negative control that only appends an ignore line was rejected: vsce lets `!bundled/**/*` re-include the file whatever the order, so the control also drops the !bundled lines. (4) `runner.os == 'Linux'`, which the neighbouring steps use, is equivalent today, but the DoD names ubuntu-latest. (5) Running onboarding before the check was rejected: the check first fails in seconds with a named path.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: vsce 4.0.0 ignore semantics are order-insensitive, and negations win (mem:gotcha-vsce-vscodeignore-negations-win). release.yml already runs this onboarding on the vsix, but only at release. VSC-16's bundler fails before packaging on any missing manifest source, so the CI check guards the vsce/.vscodeignore side and the staged-vs-shipped gap. Planning dry runs: 4089 files and 61.3 MB at 3cfc3c78; at ff56d4ff all 16 targets are present, the only dist/ entry is extension.js, and 8 dependency eslint.config.js files under bundled/daemon/node_modules are expected and unaffected.
planningNotes.risks: Onboarding's 20 s restart-health deadline can trip on slow disks (seen once on drvfs; ext4 is fine, and the CI runner is ext4). A future vsce upgrade could change ignore semantics: checkRefs 4 and 5 would then fail loudly, not silently. The snapshot needs npm registry access and about 0.8 GB per run. ci.yml may later be edited by gate-held rows (task-b6a3d41e and others); in worktree mode non-overlapping hunks merge.
